name: cc-enforcer
description: Rules your coding agent physically cannot ignore. A Claude Code plugin (and LLM-agnostic rule pack) that stops reactive patching, guessed citations, surface-level fixes and premature "done" claims by intercepting the agent's own tool calls — PreToolUse denies the edit before it lands, and a nine-layer Stop gate refuses to let a completion claim end the turn without evidence, a convergence self-quiz, a fidelity check against the original request, and a one-line TL;DR. Twelve rules, eight of them backed by a hook; per-project "Imperial Edict" regexes you define yourself; a repo-wide sync gate; three CI drift gates that derive every documented number from the code so the docs cannot rot. Zero dependencies, stdlib only, and every guard fails OPEN — a bug in the discipline can never brick your agent. v0.35.0 makes the cap-type limits relative to the thing they limit. The rolling-patch counter's "systematic rewrite" bar was two absolute numbers (>= 1500 chars OR >= 50 lines) compared against a file whose size the classifier never looked at -- so on any file below both, NO edit could ever reach it: a full Write of a 30-line module lands in "medium", which neither counts nor resets, and three small edits locked that file for the rest of the session with one legal move left, padding it past 1500 characters. A gate against reactive patching, demanding the file be made bigger. A change now also qualifies as systematic by SPANNING >= 30% of its target on either axis; the floors are kept, so the change is monotone-loosening and nothing systematic before stops being systematic now. Re-scaling both ends instead (max(1500, 30% of file)) was rejected because it raises the floor for large files and recreates the identical lock-in at the other end. Two shapes are now never counted at all: a NET REDUCTION (len(new) < len(old)) -- a rolling patch is an accretion, and an edit leaving the file shorter than it found it is the opposite of what this layer stops -- and a BOOKKEEPING edit, where both sides are byte-identical once numeric runs are elided and every moved number holds the same bookkeeping shape on both sides (version, ISO date; bare integers too in prose docs). That allowlist is shaped rather than "any digit" precisely because timeout = 30 -> 300 and if n > 3 -> n > 4 are also small numeric edits, and rule 09 names lengthening a timeout and loosening an assertion as forbidden. Third, Stop layer (h)'s tldr cap now counts DISPLAY COLUMNS rather than code points, and the root cause was sitting in the constant's own comment, which conceded in passing that "a full English sentence fits; a Chinese sentence is far shorter" -- one number meaning two things on the two halves of a bilingual contract, with the zh side about twice as loose. CJK counts 2, combining marks 0, ASCII unchanged. The classification logic moved into lib/editscale.py, a fourth judgement model beside srclex, mdctx and shellcmd: the small-file lock-in survived twenty-two releases because the classifier was only ever reachable through a hook payload and every fixture file happened to be one line long. New bench_hooks.py measures per-hook latency against a bare-interpreter baseline, and both READMEs were restructured (name / intro / features and scope / implementation / before-after / benchmark / philosophy / limits) with the benchmark section stating plainly that no CI gate pins those numbers. 617 -> 676 tests. Prior -- v0.34.1 is a fact-alignment release: a four-agent audit read every claim in the repo (docs vs code, rules/prompts vs hook behavior, comments/docstrings vs reality) and 29 confirmed misalignments were fixed — plus ONE real bug the audit flushed out of a comment: _clip_edicts, the routine that trims the edict block when an injection exceeds the 10,000-char hook cap, keyed its entry boundary to the [Exx] line shape that manage_edicts PRINTS, while the injected block is a markdown table whose rows start with a backticked id — so the over-cap path dropped EVERY edict and the elision notice reported 0 cut, an unfounded claim in the output of the plugin built to block them. The existing test stayed green because its fixture hand-rolled the same wrong shape; it now builds the block through the real renderer, with a non-vacuity guard, an honest-count assertion, and a shape-coupling pin so a renderer change fails the suite before production reverts to drop-all-report-zero. Also fixed at the contract level: the read-before-edit DENY message's escape-hatch recipe showed two commands in one block, but the registration parser (by design, v0.27) credits only a bare single-segment command — following the printed recipe silently failed to register; the recipe now says two separate Bash calls. Injected prompts stopped over-promising detectors (user ruling: prompts align down to implementations): the hedge row now lists the shapes _HEDGE_INNER actually matches (bare should/应该 are deliberately not detected), and the rule-08 row names the six keyword groups the hook actually counts. The doc drift gate learned the mirror lesson a third time: README.zh.md's test counts sat two releases stale behind a green gate because only README.md's were registered — the zh mirror now joins the inventory, test-count and current-release-narrative surfaces. 615 -> 617 tests. Prior — v0.34.0 adds env-file hygiene: Claude Code sources CLAUDE_ENV_FILE into every Bash call, SessionStart fires on every compact/resume, and a plugin that appends its exports unconditionally on that event grows the file without bound — a real session lost every Bash call silently at ~8 KB of duplicates. The true origin (a third-party plugin's non-idempotent append) is out of reach, but the class is this plugin's remit: lib/envfile.py now dedupes the file on every SessionStart, keeping the last occurrence per variable — byte-equivalent to what sourcing already yields, so nothing observable changes, only the growth goes. Refusal over gamble: any shape the line model does not represent (non-export lines, a quoted value spanning lines) refuses the whole pass byte-identically, each acceptance case shipping with its refusal twin. 604 -> 615 tests. Prior — v0.33.0 renames the project: cc-enslaver is now cc-enforcer. Same twelve rules, same hooks, a name that says what the thing does. Everything derived from the name moves with it: the /cc-enforcer:* command namespace, the CC_ENFORCER_* environment variables, the per-project config directory .claude/cc-enforcer/{edicts,sync-gate}.toml, the install coordinate cc-enforcer@cc-enforcer, and the GitHub URL (the old one redirects). BREAKING for existing installs, deliberately without a compat shim: both config loaders are failing-open, so an unmigrated .claude/cc-enslaver/ directory does not error — it silently stops enforcing, which is exactly why the migration is one loud directory rename instead of a quiet fallback that would leave two truth locations forever. The rename also caught the defect class a rename is built to catch: two CLI sites composed the config path from their own copy of the plugin-name literal instead of the shared constant. manage_edicts --global would have WRITTEN to the old directory while the loader READ the new one, and sync-gate's path command printed a would-be location derived from the process cwd that add (which honours CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR) would never write to — the same print-vs-write divergence class as v0.31's birth defect, one command over. Both are now single definitions (lib/edicts gained a public global_path(); cmd_path prints through the deterministic write resolver), each pinned by a regression test plus the twin that keeps equality from being satisfied by two identical literals. CHANGELOG history is NOT rewritten: past entries keep the name the project shipped under, because a dated record claiming /cc-enforcer:gc existed in v0.6.1 would be a lie with a version number on it. 601 -> 604 tests. Prior — v0.32.2 answers "are all the docs updated?" by checking instead of asserting, and found two that were not. No code change. The audit that matters is the COMPLEMENT: diff the markdown touched across the release series against every markdown in the repo, then read the UNTOUCHED files for claims the releases invalidated. Both defects were in that set; neither was reachable from "did I update the README" — the README was fine. FIRST, a cross-document claim true in only one direction: commands/sync-gate.md (added v0.31.0) told the reader that the repo-refresh skill should call its `add` and close with `check`, while the skill's own Step 6 still said hand-edit the TOML, with no mention of the CLI that had existed for two releases and none of `check`. Document A asserted that document B does X; document B did not know — drift introduced by documenting a new coupling on one side only. Step 6 now carries the invocation, states that `check` is the step's convergence check rather than an optional extra (the loader is failing-open: a mistyped glob never fires and never complains), and repeats that groups are asserted by a human, never guessed. ARCHITECTURE section 8 gains the coupling as a row with the lesson: a cross-document claim IS a coupling and must be verified from BOTH ends. SECOND, docs/RULES.md’s rule-to-component table listed only lib/sync_gate.py for rule 12, so the CLI and slash command that manage its config were missing from the one table whose job is that mapping. No new gate was added for it, deliberately: test_doc_sync derives every pinned fact from the CODE, while this table maps a judgement no derivation can produce, and a gate over it would compare one hand-maintained list against another — the doc-to-doc comparison that file’s own design notes forbid. Recorded as a known uncovered surface instead of papered over with coverage-shaped decoration. 601 tests unchanged. Prior — v0.32.1 closes the project out: the roadmap is retired and the rule text catches up with what the code enforces. No behaviour change. The one that mattered: `rules/` is not internal documentation, it is the LLM-AGNOSTIC PRODUCT — `cat rules/*.md` is a documented install path for agents that do not speak Claude Code's plugin protocol — and rules/12 still described the v0.27 escape hatch after v0.32 tightened it, so a rule-pack consumer was told the hatch was looser than the hook actually is. Same class as v0.26's docstring claiming nesting was handled, one layer out; fixed in the English skeleton, the zh mirror, and commands/checklist.md at the point of use. The roadmap is now empty by decision, with both remaining entries retired in all THREE places they were listed (the third, docs/EDICTS.md, would have been missed by anyone editing only the first two): per-session ephemeral edicts are DROPPED, structurally rather than for effort — the edict CLI is a Bash subprocess with no session_id, only a hook payload carries one, which is why register_read's authoritative half lives in bash_guard — and the layer-(g) content-hash upgrade is RETIRED with its premise measured false: it assumed 1-second mtime granularity, while consecutive writes on this plugin's primary platform are distinguishable at 1 ms and layer (g) compares a first-encounter baseline against closing time, seconds apart, three orders of magnitude clear of the collision window. Reopen on a reproduction, not a hypothesis. 601 tests unchanged. Prior — v0.32.0 closes the two items v0.31 recorded instead of fixing, both decided by the user. FIRST, Stop layer (i) now rejects a sync acknowledgement that answers nothing: `_has_sync_marker` was presence-only, so `sync-check: n/a` — and a marker the agent merely QUOTED — settled a named co-update group as firmly as a real sweep report. It now applies the two tests layer (h) already applies to `tldr`, through the same lib/mdctx model: attribution (a marker inside a non-canonical fence or a blockquote is illustrative, not a claim) and substance (the value must carry content, on its own line or the next non-blank one; a bare placeholder is treated as absent, and a non-answer cannot borrow the following line). The limit is pinned by its own test so it cannot drift into an implied guarantee: vacuous PROSE (`sync-check: checked it`) is still accepted and is not claimed to be detected, because refusing an honest report is the worse error. A deliberate strictness increase. SECOND, `check` now runs against this repository in CI. v0.31.0 shipped it arguing that an unenforced gate you still trust is worse than none, and gave it a non-zero exit specifically so it could run in CI — then never ran it on itself, the same defect one level up. Wired as a test rather than a workflow step, matching test_i18n_sync, so a local unittest run covers it too, and shipped with the twin that keeps a green check from meaning an empty config. 594 -> 601 tests. Prior — v0.31.1 folds rule 12's acknowledgement into the reply schema. Every other closing obligation (before / edits / convergence / fidelity / closing / tldr) has been a schema FIELD since v0.20, whose design is that the field name IS the Stop-hook marker; rule 12 arrived three releases later and its sync acknowledgement stayed free prose with no slot to write it in — the only duty whose omission looked like an ordinary reply. It is now `sync-check:` (zh: `同步核对:`) in all four injected prompts. Zero hook code changed: the key already matches SYNC_MARKERS. It does NOT weaken layer (i), verified by probe rather than by reading — since v0.27 a marker settles only groups a previous block actually NAMED, so a first violation still blocks and names its group, and the field is where the answer to that group goes next turn. A vacuous `sync-check: n/a` still settles a named group; that is unchanged from today's free-prose markers, is called out in both prompts, and adding a substance check would be a strictness contract change deliberately not made here. The release also found a pre-existing drift: README.zh.md's version badge said 0.29.0 at 0.31.1 — two releases stale with every gate green — because the badge check pinned README.md and not its mirror; it now discovers every README*.md from disk. 590 -> 594 tests. Prior — v0.31.0 made the rule-12 sync gate INSPECTABLE. Co-update groups have been enforceable since v0.23 and authorable only by hand-writing TOML, with no way to see what the loader made of it — and the loader is failing-open by design, so a dropped group or a glob matching no file does not raise, it just stops guarding while printing one stderr line nobody reads. An unenforced gate you still trust is worse than no gate, because you have stopped looking. The new `/cc-enforcer:sync-gate` command (init / list / check / add / remove / path) closes that: `check` reports every group the loader kept, every group it DROPPED and why, and every dead glob, exiting 1 so it runs in CI. Deliberately NOT auto-created — no hook writes into your project directory, and an auto-created empty template would be functionally identical to no file (zero groups means layer (i) stays inert) at the price of an unrequested file in everyone's git status. Writes are verified twice: not just "does this parse" but "does the loader still keep every group", because a `require = []` entry is valid TOML that load() silently discards, so a parse-only check would let the CLI report success over a group guarding nothing; on failure the previous file is restored byte-for-byte. A defect found in this feature's own first smoke test is reported rather than quietly fixed: the CLI picked its write target with the resolver built for READING, which tries several roots and takes the first that already holds a file — so run against a project with no config yet it fell through to the process cwd and wrote two groups into this plugin's own config. Root cause: "where do I read from" and "where do I write to" are different questions, and a read-resolver's fallback chain is exactly what makes it the wrong answer to the second. Fixed at the mechanism (default_project_path, deterministic; load_file, no fallback), class swept across both call sites, with the read resolver's fallback pinned too so a later "make everything deterministic" cannot silently break the hook path. lib/tomlio.py now owns the TOML writer as well as the reader, so both config CLIs share one encoder. 565 → 590 tests. Prior — v0.30.0 was a structural audit of the plugin itself, on one theme: a thing that is written down is not a thing that is enforced. Seven unreachable production symbols were deleted rather than annotated — including a retired rationale checker sitting beside the live one, where the next reader cannot tell which the guard consults, and an `_escape_triple_quoted` marked "kept only so an external caller does not break" that no caller could reach. Three duplicated judgements collapsed to one definition each: markdown fence parsing existed in three copies, each carrying its own transcription of the same v0.25 CommonMark fix, and the project-root predicate existed twice with the second annotated "same heuristic as lib/edicts.py" — a sentence that names an invariant without holding it (new: lib/projroot.py). And the Stop status table stopped lying: layers are displayed (a)-(i) but evaluated with (b) first, and the table derived both Pass and pending from the DISPLAY index, so every hedge block printed "(a) PASS" — asserting convergence evidence had been found on a turn where the evidence check never ran. A gate built to catch unfounded claims does not get to make one; fixed with twin tests in both directions. The tree was reclassified rather than rearranged (test files named for what they cover, hooks/scripts/ labelling its three roles inline, a new docs/ index), and the four non-hook scripts deliberately did NOT move to a tools/ directory: two of them are called from inside hooks, so the move would trade a tidier directory name for a real cross-tree import splice. CLAUDE.md shrank 87 KB to 39 KB — its "current version" section had become a verbatim second copy of the changelog, re-read into context on every session, and a second source that could drift. 564 → 565 tests. Full history: CHANGELOG.md.
